Hi Laura — great to hear the pilot went well with your team. See three pragmatic structures below; I'll surface the economics and contract language after you flag a preferred direction.

Option A — Minimal-commit ramp (best for cash conservation)
- 6-month initial term (applied inside a 24-month master), small committed baseline for Q1.
- Monthly metered overage; surge capacity available as on-demand at a higher per-token rate.
- At month 7, auto-convert to annual billing at agreed uplift if usage trend crosses threshold.

Option B — Safety-net band (recommended for predictable scale)
- 24-month master agreement with staged committed buckets (Q1 baseline -> Q2 2x -> remaining term variable).
- Surge band: short-term reserved burst pool (e.g., 1-4 weeks) that can be invoked up to N tokens/month; pre-authorized charge mechanism or a small committed escrow to avoid procurement delays.
- Co-terming: all modules consolidate to the same renewal date at the end of year one with a single renewal invoice.

Option C — Upfront convertible credit (best pricing, moderate commitment)
- One-time credit purchase applied against utilization; unused credit rolls into year two under a 12-month usage carve-out.
- Surge priced at a discounted rate if you keep a minimum committed band.

A few clarifying Qs to help narrow:
1) Do you need an immediate contractual cap on surge spend (hard limit) or prefer alerts + soft caps?
2) Is procurement okay with a small escrow or PO that activates bursts, or would you prefer purely post-pay?

I'll draft a redlineable contract stub for Option B (since it trades predictability and speed to scale) and loop in pricing.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
